subproblem.title: Difference quotients converge uniformly on closed balls at a point of differentiability
subproblem.statement: Let n, k ∈ ℕ, f : ℝⁿ → ℝᵏ (ℝⁿ = Euclid n with the Euclidean norm) and v ∈ ℝⁿ, and suppose f is differentiable at v, with Fréchet derivative T := Df(v) (Mathlib fderiv ℝ f v). Then for every R ∈ ℝ, the difference quotients f_{v,r}(w) := r⁻¹(f(v + rw) − f(v)) converge to T w uniformly for w ∈ closedBall(0, R) as r ↓ 0. That is, for every ε > 0 there is a set S belonging to the filter 𝓝[>] 0 such that |T w − f_{v,r}(w)| < ε for all r ∈ S and all w with |w| ≤ R.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n k : ℕ) (f : Euclid n → Euclid k) (v : Euclid n), DifferentiableAt ℝ f v → ∀ R : ℝ, TendstoUniformlyOn (fun (r : ℝ) (w : Euclid n) => r⁻¹ • (f (v + r • w) - f v)) (fun w => fderiv ℝ f v w) (𝓝[>] 0) (closedBall (0 : Euclid n) R)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the o(|h|) estimate in Step 8 of the parent proof (`weighted_blowup_limit`). That step shows |f_{v,r}(w) − T_v w| ≤ δ/2 on closedBall(0, R) for 0 < r < ρ/R. Here it is isolated as a uniform-convergence statement on an arbitrary closed ball. Notation: ℝⁿ = Euclid n with Euclidean norm |·|, T := Df(v) = fderiv ℝ f v, f_{v,r}(w) := r⁻¹(f(v + rw) − f(v)).
1. (Reformulation.) By the metric characterization of uniform convergence on a set (Mathlib `Metric.tendstoUniformlyOn_iff`), it suffices to show the following: for every ε > 0 there is a set S belonging to 𝓝[>] 0 such that dist(T w, f_{v,r}(w)) = |T w − f_{v,r}(w)| < ε for all r ∈ S and all w ∈ closedBall(0, R). Fix ε > 0.
2. (Auxiliary radius.) Put R' := max(R, 1). Then R' ≥ 1 > 0, and every w ∈ closedBall(0, R) satisfies |w| ≤ R ≤ R'. (If R < 0 the ball is empty; the argument needs no case distinction.)
3. (Little-o bound.) Since f is differentiable at v, it has Fréchet derivative T at v, i.e. f(v + h) − f(v) − T h = o(|h|) as h → 0 (Mathlib `DifferentiableAt.hasFDerivAt`, `hasFDerivAt_iff_isLittleO_nhds_zero`). Apply the little-o bound with the constant c := ε/(2R') > 0 (Mathlib `Asymptotics.IsLittleO.bound`). This gives |f(v + h) − f(v) − T h| ≤ c|h| for all h in a neighbourhood of 0. By `Metric.eventually_nhds_iff` there is ρ > 0 such that this holds whenever dist(h, 0) = |h| < ρ. (Lean note: do not write `IsLittleO.def`; the word `def` is rejected by the machine-leaf source check even inside a proof.)
4. (The set S.) Let S := (0, ρ/R'). As ρ/R' > 0, S ∈ 𝓝[>] 0 (Mathlib `Ioo_mem_nhdsGT`). Fix r ∈ S, so 0 < r < ρ/R', and fix w ∈ closedBall(0, R).
5. (rw is small.) |rw| = r|w| ≤ rR' < (ρ/R')·R' = ρ. Hence Step 3 applies to h = rw: |f(v + rw) − f(v) − T(rw)| ≤ c|rw| = c·r·|w|.
6. (Algebraic identity.) T is linear, so T(rw) = r·T w, and r⁻¹·r = 1 because r ≠ 0. Therefore T w − f_{v,r}(w) = −r⁻¹·(f(v + rw) − f(v) − T(rw)). (Lean: `simp only [map_smul, smul_sub, smul_smul, inv_mul_cancel₀ hr.ne', one_smul]` followed by `abel` proves it.)
7. (Estimate.) By Steps 5 and 6, |T w − f_{v,r}(w)| = r⁻¹·|f(v + rw) − f(v) − T(rw)| ≤ r⁻¹·c·r·|w| = c|w| ≤ c·R' = ε/2 < ε.
8. (Conclusion.) For all r ∈ S and all w ∈ closedBall(0, R) we have dist(T w, f_{v,r}(w)) < ε, and S ∈ 𝓝[>] 0. Since ε > 0 was arbitrary, Step 1 shows that f_{v,r} → T uniformly on closedBall(0, R) as r ↓ 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Reduce via Metric.tendstoUniformlyOn_iff to: for every ε > 0, eventually as r ↓ 0, |T w − f_{v,r}(w)| < ε for all w ∈ closedBall(0, R).
Put R' = max(R, 1). Differentiability at v (little-o) gives ρ > 0 with |f(v + h) − f(v) − T h| ≤ (ε/(2R'))|h| whenever |h| < ρ.
For 0 < r < ρ/R' and |w| ≤ R: |rw| < ρ, so by linearity |T w − f_{v,r}(w)| = r⁻¹|f(v + rw) − f(v) − T(rw)| ≤ (ε/(2R'))|w| ≤ ε/2 < ε.

The proof derives the little-o estimate from differentiability, chooses R′ = max(R, 1), and obtains the uniform ε/2 bound for 0 < r < ρ/R′ using linearity and positive-scalar norm identities. Negative-radius balls and zero-dimensional spaces cause no gap. No child or parent theorem is assumed.

subproblem.title: Ball integrals of test-function differences along graph blow-ups tend to zero
subproblem.statement: Let n, k ∈ ℕ. Let ι : ℝⁿ → ℝ^{n+k} and ι' : ℝᵏ → ℝ^{n+k} be linear isometries. Let f : ℝⁿ → ℝᵏ be continuous and differentiable at v ∈ ℝⁿ, with T := Df(v) (Mathlib fderiv ℝ f v). Let ψ : ℝ^{n+k} → ℝ be continuous with compact support, and let R ∈ ℝ. Then, with Lⁿ the Lebesgue measure (volume) on ℝⁿ, U(r) := ∫_{closedBall(0,R)} |ψ(ιw + ι'(r⁻¹(f(v + rw) − f(v)))) − ψ(ιw + ι'(T w))| dLⁿ(w) → 0 as r ↓ 0 (along 𝓝[>] 0).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n k : ℕ) (ι : Euclid n →ₗᵢ[ℝ] Euclid (n + k)) (ι' : Euclid k →ₗᵢ[ℝ] Euclid (n + k)) (f : Euclid n → Euclid k) (v : Euclid n) (ψ : Euclid (n + k) → ℝ), Continuous f → DifferentiableAt ℝ f v → Continuous ψ → HasCompactSupport ψ → ∀ R : ℝ, Tendsto (fun r : ℝ => ∫ w in closedBall (0 : Euclid n) R, |ψ (ι w + ι' (r⁻¹ • (f (v + r • w) - f v))) - ψ (ι w + ι' (fderiv ℝ f v w))|) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 8 of the parent proof (`weighted_blowup_limit`). There ψ is uniformly continuous and f_{v,r} → T_v uniformly on the ball, hence 0 ≤ U(r) ≤ ε'·Lⁿ(B) < ε for small r > 0. Notation: Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ, B := closedBall(0, R), T := Df(v) = fderiv ℝ f v, f_{v,r}(w) := r⁻¹(f(v + rw) − f(v)), Φ_r(w) := ιw + ι'(f_{v,r}(w)), Φ(w) := ιw + ι'(T w), Δ_r(w) := |ψ(Φ_r(w)) − ψ(Φ(w))|, U(r) := ∫_B Δ_r dLⁿ.
1. (The integrand.) For each r, Φ_r and Φ are continuous: f is continuous, ι, ι' and T are continuous linear maps, and w ↦ v + rw is continuous. So Δ_r is continuous, hence Borel measurable, with 0 ≤ Δ_r ≤ 2·sup|ψ| < ∞. Thus U(r) is a well-defined real number, and U(r) ≥ 0 because the integrand is nonnegative (Mathlib `integral_nonneg`). (Lean note: the Mathlib estimates used below need no measurability, so the hypothesis `Continuous f` may be introduced unused, e.g. as `_hf`.)
2. (Graph maps converge uniformly.) Apply the sibling `diff_quotient_uniform` (Lean: `Submission.dorwbl_diff_quotient_tendstoUniformlyOn` applied to n, k, f, v, the differentiability of f at v, and R). It gives f_{v,r} → T uniformly on B as r ↓ 0. For all r and w, Φ(w) − Φ_r(w) = ι'(T w − f_{v,r}(w)), since the ιw terms cancel and ι' is linear. Also |ι'(x)| = |x| because ι' is a linear isometry. Hence dist(Φ(w), Φ_r(w)) = dist(T w, f_{v,r}(w)). Using `Metric.tendstoUniformlyOn_iff` in both directions, Φ_r → Φ uniformly on B as r ↓ 0. (Lean: inside `filter_upwards`, rewrite with `dist_eq_norm`, `add_sub_add_left_eq_sub`, `← map_sub`, `LinearIsometry.norm_map`.)
3. (Composition with ψ.) A continuous function with compact support is uniformly continuous (Mathlib `HasCompactSupport.uniformContinuous_of_continuous`). Composing a uniformly convergent family with a uniformly continuous map preserves uniform convergence (Mathlib `UniformContinuous.comp_tendstoUniformlyOn`). Hence ψ∘Φ_r → ψ∘Φ uniformly on B: for every η > 0 there is S_η ∈ 𝓝[>] 0 such that |ψ(Φ(w)) − ψ(Φ_r(w))| < η, i.e. Δ_r(w) < η, for all r ∈ S_η and all w ∈ B.
4. (Finite measure.) B is compact, so Lⁿ(B) < ∞ (Mathlib `measure_closedBall_lt_top`). Let V := Lⁿ(B) ∈ [0, ∞), viewed as a real number (`volume.real B`).
5. (ε-step.) Let ε > 0, put η := ε/(V + 1) > 0, and let r ∈ S_η. For every w ∈ B, |Δ_r(w)| = Δ_r(w) ≤ η. The constant-bound estimate for set integrals over a set of finite measure (Mathlib `norm_setIntegral_le_of_norm_le_const`) then gives |U(r)| ≤ η·V. Because εV < εV + ε = ε(V + 1), we have η·V = εV/(V + 1) < ε. Together with U(r) ≥ 0 (Step 1), dist(U(r), 0) = U(r) ≤ ηV < ε.
6. (Conclusion.) For every ε > 0, dist(U(r), 0) < ε for all r in the set S_{ε/(V+1)} ∈ 𝓝[>] 0. By the metric characterization of limits (Mathlib `Metric.tendsto_nhds`), U(r) → 0 as r ↓ 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: By `diff_quotient_uniform`, f_{v,r} → Df(v) uniformly on B = closedBall(0, R). Since ι' is a linear isometry, dist(Φ(w), Φ_r(w)) = dist(Df(v)w, f_{v,r}(w)), so Φ_r → Φ uniformly on B.
ψ is uniformly continuous (continuous with compact support), so ψ∘Φ_r → ψ∘Φ uniformly on B.
Given ε > 0, put η = ε/(Lⁿ(B) + 1). Eventually Δ_r ≤ η on B, so 0 ≤ U(r) ≤ η·Lⁿ(B) < ε by norm_setIntegral_le_of_norm_le_const; hence U(r) → 0.

audit.reason: The proposition includes all stated hypotheses and the correct restricted-volume integral. The proof uses only its declared predecessor: the isometry transfers uniform convergence to graph maps, uniform continuity transfers it through ψ, and the finite-measure estimate with η = ε/(volume.real B + 1) proves convergence of the integral. Continuity and boundedness justify integrability; empty balls are covered. The supplied argument is complete and directly formalizable.

subproblem.title: Weighted graph blow-up integrals converge at a differentiability point that is a rescaled Lebesgue point of the weight
subproblem.statement: Let n, k ∈ ℕ. Let ι : ℝⁿ → ℝ^{n+k} and ι' : ℝᵏ → ℝ^{n+k} be linear isometries with ⟨ιx, ι'y⟩ = 0 for all x ∈ ℝⁿ, y ∈ ℝᵏ. Let f : ℝⁿ → ℝᵏ be continuous. Let C ∈ ℝ and let G : ℝⁿ → ℝ be Borel measurable with |G(u)| ≤ C for all u. Let v ∈ ℝⁿ be such that f is differentiable at v, with T := Df(v) (Mathlib fderiv ℝ f v), and such that for every R > 0, ∫_{closedBall(0,R)} |G(v + rw) − G(v)| dLⁿ(w) → 0 as r ↓ 0 (Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ). Then for every continuous compactly supported ψ : ℝ^{n+k} → ℝ, ∫_{ℝⁿ} ψ(ιw + ι'(r⁻¹(f(v + rw) − f(v))))·G(v + rw) dLⁿ(w) → G(v)·∫_{ℝⁿ} ψ(ιw + ι'(T w)) dLⁿ(w) as r ↓ 0 (along 𝓝[>] 0).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n k : ℕ) (ι : Euclid n →ₗᵢ[ℝ] Euclid (n + k)) (ι' : Euclid k →ₗᵢ[ℝ] Euclid (n + k)) (f : Euclid n → Euclid k) (G : Euclid n → ℝ) (C : ℝ) (v : Euclid n), (∀ x y, inner ℝ (ι x) (ι' y) = 0) → Continuous f → Measurable G → (∀ u, |G u| ≤ C) → DifferentiableAt ℝ f v → (∀ R : ℝ, 0 < R → Tendsto (fun r : ℝ => ∫ w in closedBall (0 : Euclid n) R, |G (v + r • w) - G v|) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0)) → ∀ ψ : Euclid (n + k) → ℝ, Continuous ψ → HasCompactSupport ψ → Tendsto (fun r : ℝ => ∫ w, ψ (ι w + ι' (r⁻¹ • (f (v + r • w) - f v))) * G (v + r • w)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (G v * ∫ w, ψ (ι w + ι' (fderiv ℝ f v w))))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 2–7 and 9 of the parent proof (`weighted_blowup_limit`), carried out at one fixed good point v. Step 8 of that proof is supplied by the sibling `test_integral_vanish`. The parent's Step 1 (choice of v) is replaced by the hypotheses. Notation: Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ, T := Df(v), f_{v,r}(w) := r⁻¹(f(v + rw) − f(v)), Φ_r(w) := ιw + ι'(f_{v,r}(w)), Φ(w) := ιw + ι'(T w), a_r(w) := ψ(Φ_r(w))·G(v + rw), b(w) := ψ(Φ(w))·G(v), Δ_r(w) := |ψ(Φ_r(w)) − ψ(Φ(w))|, g_r(w) := |G(v + rw) − G(v)|.
1. (Constants.) Fix ψ continuous with compact support. Then ψ is bounded: there is M with |ψ(y)| ≤ M for all y (Mathlib `HasCompactSupport.exists_bound_of_continuous`); in particular M ≥ |ψ(0)| ≥ 0. The set tsupport ψ is compact, hence bounded, so tsupport ψ ⊆ closedBall(0, R₀) for some R₀ ∈ ℝ (Mathlib `IsCompact.isBounded`, `Bornology.IsBounded.subset_closedBall`). Put R := max(R₀, 1), so R > 0 and R₀ ≤ R, and put B := closedBall(0, R) ⊆ ℝⁿ. Also C ≥ |G(0)| ≥ 0, and Lⁿ(B) < ∞ because B is compact (Mathlib `measure_closedBall_lt_top`).
2. (Pythagoras.) For w ∈ ℝⁿ and u ∈ ℝᵏ: |ιw + ι'u|² = |ιw|² + 2⟨ιw, ι'u⟩ + |ι'u|² = |w|² + 0 + |u|² ≥ |w|². This uses Mathlib `norm_add_sq_real`, the orthogonality hypothesis and `LinearIsometry.norm_map`. Since both norms are ≥ 0, |w| ≤ |ιw + ι'u|.
3. (Localization.) Let w ∉ B, i.e. |w| > R, and let u ∈ ℝᵏ. By Step 2, |ιw + ι'u| ≥ |w| > R ≥ R₀, so ιw + ι'u ∉ closedBall(0, R₀) ⊇ tsupport ψ. Hence ψ(ιw + ι'u) = 0 (Mathlib `image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport`). Taking u = f_{v,r}(w), resp. u = T w: for every r, a_r(w) = 0 and b(w) = 0 whenever w ∉ B. Mathlib `setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero` (which needs no integrability) therefore gives ∫_{ℝⁿ} a_r = ∫_B a_r. Similarly, moving the constant G(v) inside the integral and commuting the product, G(v)·∫_{ℝⁿ} ψ(Φ(w)) dw = ∫_{ℝⁿ} b = ∫_B b.
4. (The two limits.) Apply the sibling `test_integral_vanish` (Lean: `Submission.dorwbl_test_fn_diff_quotient_integral_tendsto_zero` applied to n, k, ι, ι', f, v, ψ, the continuity of f, the differentiability of f at v, the continuity and compact support of ψ, and this R). It gives U(r) := ∫_B Δ_r dLⁿ → 0 as r ↓ 0. By the hypothesis on v with this R > 0, V(r) := ∫_B g_r dLⁿ → 0 as r ↓ 0. Hence C·U(r) + M·V(r) → C·0 + M·0 = 0 as r ↓ 0. (Lean note: form this limit as `(hU.const_mul C).add (hV.const_mul M)` and then `rw [mul_zero, mul_zero, add_zero] at` it. Do not use `simpa using` here: simp rewrites `ι' (r⁻¹ • (…))` into `r⁻¹ • (ι' … - ι' …)`, and the later integral rewrites then fail to match.)
5. (Measurability and integrability on B; fix r > 0.) Φ_r and Φ are continuous (f continuous; ι, ι', T continuous linear; w ↦ v + rw continuous), so ψ∘Φ_r and ψ∘Φ are continuous (in Lean, `fun_prop` proves this). The map w ↦ G(v + rw) is Borel measurable, as a measurable G composed with a continuous map. Hence a_r, b, Δ_r and g_r are measurable (Lean: `Measurable.abs` is not available; use `continuous_abs.measurable.comp (…)`). They are bounded by M·C, M·C, 2M and 2C respectively. A bounded measurable function on a set of finite measure is integrable there (Mathlib `Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded`). So a_r, b, Δ_r and g_r, and hence C·Δ_r + M·g_r, are integrable on B.
6. (Pointwise bound.) For every w: a_r(w) − b(w) = [ψ(Φ_r(w)) − ψ(Φ(w))]·G(v + rw) + ψ(Φ(w))·[G(v + rw) − G(v)] (ring identity). By the triangle inequality, |G| ≤ C and |ψ| ≤ M: |a_r(w) − b(w)| ≤ Δ_r(w)·|G(v + rw)| + |ψ(Φ(w))|·g_r(w) ≤ C·Δ_r(w) + M·g_r(w).
7. (Integral bound.) Let r > 0. By Step 3 and linearity of the integral (a_r and b are integrable on B by Step 5), ∫_{ℝⁿ} a_r − G(v)·∫_{ℝⁿ} ψ∘Φ = ∫_B a_r − ∫_B b = ∫_B (a_r − b). By Step 6 and the integrability of C·Δ_r + M·g_r on B (Mathlib `norm_integral_le_of_norm_le`), |∫_B (a_r − b)| ≤ ∫_B (C·Δ_r + M·g_r) = C·U(r) + M·V(r) (Mathlib `integral_add`, `integral_const_mul`).
8. (Conclusion.) For all r in (0, ∞), a set belonging to 𝓝[>] 0 (Mathlib `self_mem_nhdsWithin`), we have 0 ≤ |∫ a_r − G(v)·∫ ψ∘Φ| ≤ C·U(r) + M·V(r). The right side tends to 0 by Step 4. By the squeeze theorem (Mathlib `squeeze_zero'`), |∫ a_r − G(v)·∫ ψ∘Φ| → 0. By Mathlib `tendsto_iff_norm_sub_tendsto_zero`, this means ∫ ψ(Φ_r(w))·G(v + rw) dw → G(v)·∫ ψ(Φ(w)) dw as r ↓ 0. Since ψ was arbitrary, the statement is proved. (Lean note: everything is one theorem; do not add helper declarations or options.) ∎
proof_key_steps: Bound |ψ| ≤ M and put tsupport ψ ⊆ closedBall(0, R₀), R := max(R₀, 1) > 0, B := closedBall(0, R).
Pythagoras |ιw + ι'u| ≥ |w| (orthogonal isometries) makes a_r and b vanish off B, so ∫a_r = ∫_B a_r and G(v)∫ψ∘Φ = ∫_B b.
All integrands are bounded and measurable on the finite-measure ball B, hence integrable there. Pointwise, |a_r − b| ≤ C·|ψ∘Φ_r − ψ∘Φ| + M·|G(v + r·) − G(v)|.
Hence |∫a_r − G(v)∫ψ∘Φ| ≤ C·U(r) + M·V(r) for r > 0. U(r) → 0 by `test_integral_vanish` and V(r) → 0 by the Lebesgue-point hypothesis; conclude by squeeze.

audit.reason: The exact proposition matches every hypothesis and quantifier in the prose. Orthogonality proves localization; bounded measurable integrands are integrable on the finite-measure ball; the algebraic splitting gives C·U(r) + M·V(r), which tends to zero by the declared child and the Lebesgue-point hypothesis. Squeeze proves the stated limit without circularity. Rademacher and bounded-weight local integrability then assemble the selected parent on a single full-measure set valid for every ψ.
